method.method_draft: First read the two photos as two lists of adjacent adult-child pairs: top photo has A-d, B-a, C-b, D-c, E-e; bottom photo has A-b, B-e, C-d, D-a, E-c. From the text, exactly 2 top-photo pairs and exactly 3 bottom-photo pairs are real mother-child pairs. Since there are exactly 5 real pairs total and the two photo lists have no repeated adult-child pair, all real pairs must be among these ten displayed adjacencies. Therefore each adult must choose one of its two displayed children. Enumerate which 2 adults use their top-photo child among the 5 adults, checking that the resulting 5 children are all distinct. The only valid choice is top pairs A-d and C-b, together with bottom pairs B-e, D-a, and E-c. Hence child a belongs to D.

method.method_draft: Begin by reading from the image that child a appears next to B in the first photo and next to D in the second photo. The text says the first photo contributes exactly 2 true mother-child adjacencies and the second contributes exactly 3, for 5 total true adjacencies, equal to the number of families. Thus child a's true mother must be either B or D, because every true pair must appear in one of the two photos. Test the alternative that a is B's child. Then B-a uses one of the two true first-photo positions, and D-a cannot be true in the second photo. Also B-e cannot be true because B would already have child a. To reach 3 true pairs in the second photo, the remaining second-photo pairs A-b, C-d, and E-c would all have to be true. But then no consistent additional first-photo true pair can be added without reusing an adult or child, and one adult-child assignment would be forced outside the displayed true pairs, contradicting the count exhaustion. Therefore B is impossible, so a must be D's child.

In the first photo above, the labels of the adult kangaroos and the little kangaroos beside them are, in order, A-d, B-a, C-b, D-c, E-e. In the second photo below, the corresponding adjacent labels are A-b, B-e, C-d, D-a, E-c. Reasoning: The problem says that in the first photo exactly 2 children are standing beside their own mothers, and in the second photo exactly 3 children are standing beside their own mothers. The adult-child adjacent combinations listed in the two photos have no repetition, and the real mother-child pairings are exactly 5 pairs in total, so these 2+3=5 real pairings must all come from these ten adjacent combinations. Therefore each adult kangaroo's child can only be chosen from the two children adjacent to it in the two photos. If the adult kangaroos whose real pairings are chosen from the upper photo are exactly 2, after enumeration, only when A-d and C-b are chosen as the upper real pairings, and the remaining B, D, E take the lower pairings B-e, D-a, E-c, are the five children d, b, e, a, c all different. Thus child a corresponds to adult kangaroo D.
